item.title: Generating a random numeric code in Ruby
item.description: If you work in web development, you’ve almost certainly had to generate random numeric codes like OTPs for logins or transaction verifications sent via SMS or email. It seems like a straightforward task, and your first instinct might be to reach for Kernel#rand. But that method isn’t designed for cryptographically secure random numbers, so the documentation advises switching to a safer alternative: SecureRandom#rand. Next comes requirements that can vary depending on the use case: do all ten digits need to be included in the code, do you need to exclude certain numbers, or do you need to mix in alphanumeric characters.
